# Xade

> Xade (X-provider Agentic Development Environment, pronounced "zade") is a native desktop app, written in Rust, for running AI coding agents side by side or as one multi-model team. It drives the agent CLIs you already have installed and logged in: Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity. 100% free and open source (MIT), with no subscription or API keys required. macOS and Linux.

- Website: https://xade.pro/
- Source code: https://github.com/juliomatcom/xade
- Download: https://github.com/juliomatcom/xade/releases/latest
- Install: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/juliomatcom/xade/main/scripts/install.sh | sh

## Key facts
- Runs multiple Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity sessions in side-by-side windows; sessions are saved locally (SQLite) and searchable. Existing Claude Code and Codex sessions are imported.
- Multi-Session: a team of models, from one or several providers, in one window and one working folder. The user messages all members or one with `#handle:`. Normal replies are shown only to the user; `<broadcast>` blocks reach the teammates. A Team feed plus a tab per member, Stop All, and a pause after 12 broadcast rounds in a row. Guide: https://github.com/juliomatcom/xade/blob/main/docs/multi-session.md
- Forks a session to another provider: the source agent writes a short state summary and the new one continues from it.
- The top bar shows usage quota for providers that report it.
- Uses your existing CLI login, settings, CLAUDE.md files, MCP servers, skills and permission rules. No API keys to paste; Xade never reads your credentials.
- Side-by-side diff review for every change, with per-session auto-approve.
- No telemetry; session history is saved locally. The agents still send prompts and code to their model providers.
- Model and effort picker, context and token meters, git branch and changed-file count in the bottom bar.
- Native Rust binary rendered on the GPU. No Electron.
- Coming soon: OpenCode and local models.
- Platforms: macOS (Apple Silicon), Linux (x86_64, aarch64).
